home.heroTitle: Every listing verified. Every seller real.
home.heroSubtitle: The trust-first way to buy, sell and rent property in Northern Cyprus — from first viewing to key handover.
home.step1Body: Everything in the results has cleared document checks. There is no unverified tier you have to filter out.
home.step2Title: See the deed type up front
home.step2Body: Turkish, Exchange, Allocation or Foreign is shown on every listing, next to the checks it passed.
home.step3Title: Move in one tracked deal room
home.step3Body: Viewings, contracts, deposit and handover happen in one place, with every step recorded for both sides.
home.whyTitle: Anyone can post a property. Almost nobody checks one.
home.whyBody: In Northern Cyprus the same home can sit on five sites at three prices months after it sold, and the type of title deed quietly changes what you are actually buying. Buyers are left to work that out alone, usually in a language and a legal system that isn't theirs. So we do the checking first, and publish only what passes.

deed.question: Is the deed real, and what kind is it?
deed.answerBody: Every resale listing is backed by an uploaded title deed. Our team tags it Turkish, Exchange, Allocation or Foreign, and that tag is printed on the listing, because the type decides what you are buying.

seller.question: Does this person have the right to sell it?
seller.answerTitle: We match the name on the deed
seller.answerBody: Owners upload ID that has to match the deed. Agents add a licence and a signed owner mandate; agencies and developers add company registration and construction permits. A profile that fails cannot list at all.

stale.question: Is it even still on the market?
stale.answerBody: Every 90 days the lister has to confirm the property is still available. If they don't, it drops out of search automatically, so every result you see is one somebody stood behind this quarter.

home.whyFooter: Verification is a documentary check, not legal advice or a guarantee of title. We tell you exactly what we saw, and we still recommend your own lawyer before you sign.

deeds.title: Title deeds in this region
deeds.body: In North Cyprus the type of title deed matters more than almost anything else on a listing, and it is the thing buyers from abroad least expect. Every deed here has been checked against the listing before publication.

intro.kyrenia: Kyrenia sits between the Beşparmak mountains and the north coast, built around a horseshoe harbour and castle. It draws the largest share of international buyers on the island, with the coastal strip running west through Alsancak and Lapta and east towards Esentepe.
intro.famagusta: Famagusta pairs a walled medieval old town with a working port and a large university, so demand here splits between long-term homes and reliable student rental. The Salamis coast runs north of the city.
intro.iskele: İskele has seen the most new-build and off-plan development of any region, concentrated along Long Beach and the Bafra coast. It suits buyers who want a modern apartment near the sea and are comfortable with construction timelines.
intro.nicosia: Nicosia is the capital and the island's administrative and commercial centre, inland and away from the coast. Demand is driven by employment and universities rather than holidays, which makes it the steadiest long-term rental market in the north.
intro.guzelyurt: Güzelyurt is citrus country — an agricultural west-coast region that is quieter and more spread out than the coastal resorts. It appeals to buyers looking for land and space rather than a sea-view apartment.
intro.lefke: Lefke is a small university town in the far west, backed by mountains and known for its greenery and slow pace. It is the least developed of the six regions and the furthest from the main tourist coast.
